paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Single vs. multiple platforms as data sources over time. While most of the datasets are collected from a single source, around 2018 researchers are increasingly collecting data from multiple sources (i.e., two or more).
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets collected from single versus multiple data sources over time. The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, with each category labeled in sequence. The vertical axis represents the number of datasets, with a scale ranging from 0 to 100, marked in intervals of 20. Two categories of data sources are represented: single data sources, depicted in blue, and multiple data sources, depicted in orange. In 2012, 2013, and 2014, there is one dataset from a single source, with a height of approximately 1. In 2015, the number of single-source datasets increases to around 10. For 2016, the number rises to about 15, and in 2017, it reaches approximately 20. The number of single-source datasets continues to grow, reaching around 25 in 2018, approximately 50 in 2019, about 90 in 2020, nearly 110 in 2021, and around 30 in 2022. Meanwhile, the number of datasets from multiple sources remains minimal until 2017, when it starts to increase, reaching around 10 in 2017, approximately 20 in 2018, about 20 in 2019, around 45 in 2020, nearly 50 in 2021, and approximately 10 in 2022. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, aside from being grouped by year, and no bars are visually emphasized.
